headline: The button accordion is San Antonio's instrument, and the Spurs live inside its music
summary: San Antonio music is a Mexican-American lineage: conjunto, orquesta Tejana, Chicano soul and Westside rock and R&B. It lives on in Tejano radio, dancehalls, Fiesta and a punk scene that mixes accordion with riot grrrl and garage. This is family-and-dancefloor music, and it shows up around the Spurs. Credit and partner with local musicians and poster artists instead of borrowing their look.

insights.title: Conjunto is the native sound
insights.detail: Conjunto grew up on the Westside: button accordion plus bajo sexto. The Tejano Conjunto Festival at the Guadalupe Cultural Arts Center has presented it every May for decades. Flaco Jimenez lived and worked here, won Grammys and made the accordion a global sound.
insights.implication: Treat the accordion, bajo sexto and dancehall as heritage cues. Build a Westside-rooted capsule around real players, with credit and payment. Skip the generic Mexican-American look.

insights.title: Tejano is the Spurs' family soundtrack
insights.detail: Tejano orquestas and conjuntos play quinceaneras, dancehalls, Fiesta stages and rodeo-season concerts across South Texas. The Spurs run Latin heritage nights that draw on that world, with bilingual Spanish-and-English game presentation. Selena was from Corpus Christi, but her legacy is Tejano's emotional center in San Antonio too.
insights.implication: Build around Tejano heritage nights and Selena-adjacent moments only with licensed or family-approved partners. Selena imagery is tightly controlled IP.

insights.title: Fiesta's posters and medals are a design tradition
insights.detail: April's Fiesta brings papel picado, collectible medals, royalty gowns, NIOSA and Battle of Flowers. Its poster and medal art is a long-running local design tradition. The Spurs' Fiesta-stripe City Edition already borrows the palette.
insights.implication: Extend the City Edition's colors into warm-ups, tees and headwear. Time any drop to April Fiesta and the playoff run. License the Fiesta Commission's marks.

insights.title: Westside rock and Chicano soul run rougher
insights.detail: Sunny Ozuna and Sunny & the Sunliners, the Sir Douglas Quintet and the Texas Tornados (Doug Sahm, Augie Meyers, Flaco Jimenez, Freddy Fender) fused R&B, garage rock, Tex-Mex and conjunto. Girl in a Coma and Piñata Protest carry the line into indie and punk.
insights.implication: This is the edgier counterpart to Tejano heritage. Mine it for graphics: 1960s garage-soul posters, record sleeves, lowrider-era script. Aim lifestyle product at younger, scene-literate fans.

insights.title: The military city keeps its own rhythm
insights.detail: San Antonio's four-base military community, Military City USA, lives alongside Tejano and country. Fort Sam, Lackland and Randolph families are a large part of the arena crowd. Country dancehalls like Floore's Country Store in Helotes sit next to the conjunto rooms.
insights.implication: Pair military-appreciation apparel with country and Tejano programming so it reads local. Don't reduce the market to one genre.

insights.title: The arena sounds bilingual, silver and black
insights.detail: Game presentation mixes English and Spanish. Local acts regularly play Frost Bank Center, the Alamodome and the Rodeo. With a Finals run behind them and Victor Wembanyama's French-international fan base, the building now draws more than Tejano.
insights.implication: Add a bilingual graphic layer, such as Spanish phrasing on tees. Keep a restrained silver-and-black base so the music-poster accents pop.

places.name: Guadalupe Cultural Arts Center (Guadalupe Theater)
places.why: Longtime Westside home of the Tejano Conjunto Festival and Chicano arts programming.

places.name: Majestic Theatre
places.why: A 1929 movie palace and downtown anchor, with touring and local concerts.

places.name: Tobin Center for the Performing Arts
places.why: Downtown River Walk hall and a frequent stop for Latin and Tejano touring acts. Its resident-orchestra situation changed when the San Antonio Symphony folded in 2022.

places.name: Floore's Country Store
places.why: Historic Texas country dancehall just outside the city, with country and Tejano acts.

places.name: Paper Tiger
places.why: Mid-size room for local and touring indie, punk and hip-hop.

places.name: Hogwild Records
places.why: Long-running independent record shop and touchstone of the local scene.

places.name: Alamodome
places.why: Big concerts, and the long-time setting for major Tejano events.

places.name: Frost Bank Center
places.why: Spurs home and Rodeo-season concert hall, where the team's game-night music lives.

people.name: Flaco Jimenez
people.why: San Antonio's best-known conjunto player: a Texas Tornados member and Grammy winner who died in 2025.

people.name: Selena Quintanilla
people.why: Corpus Christi's icon and the emotional center of Tejano everywhere. Her image is carefully licensed.

people.name: Lydia Mendoza
people.why: San Antonio-rooted pioneer of Mexican-American recording, and the model for generations of Tejana artists.

people.name: Sunny Ozuna
people.why: Westside voice of Sunny and the Sunliners, whose R&B-meets-Tex-Mex sound fed the Chicano soul story.

people.name: Doug Sahm and Augie Meyers
people.role: Sir Douglas Quintet and Texas Tornados musicians
people.why: San Antonio garage-rock and Tex-Mex fusion, mixing Vox-style combo organ with conjunto.

people.name: Girl in a Coma
people.why: Latina-fronted indie band that carries the city's scene to national stages.

people.name: Piñata Protest
people.why: Local band that fuses conjunto accordion with punk and pulls a younger border-Texas crowd.

people.name: Intocable
people.why: South Texas group with a huge San Antonio following and frequent arena shows.

moments.name: Fiesta San Antonio
moments.why: Ten-day citywide festival: live music stages, papel picado, medals, parades and the year's biggest design moment.

moments.name: Tejano Conjunto Festival en San Antonio
moments.why: Annual celebration of accordion-driven conjunto at the Guadalupe Cultural Arts Center.

moments.name: San Antonio Stock Show and Rodeo
moments.why: Concert-driven rodeo season at the arena, with Tejano and country headliners mid-NBA season.

moments.name: Selena remembrance
moments.why: Annual remembrance of Selena that matters to Tejano fans across South Texas.

moments.name: Dia de los Muertos celebrations
moments.why: Altars, processions and community festivals that overlap the season opener.

moments.name: Spurs Latin heritage nights
moments.timing: Select home games, typically fall to winter
moments.why: The team's route to Spanish-language, Tejano-flavored game-night programming.

designCues.source: Fiesta decorations and the City Edition's Fiesta stripe palette
designCues.use: Chest and shorts stripe accents on warm-ups and tees, tied to the City Edition.

designCues.cue: Marigold gold from cempasuchil and Fiesta royalty
designCues.source: Dia de los Muertos altars and Fiesta regalia
designCues.use: Secondary accent for trim and graphics on a black or silver base.

designCues.cue: Turquoise from papel picado banners and Westside murals
designCues.use: Third stripe color or lining detail.
Neutral anchor, so the scene colors read as accents, not costume.
Tonal jacquard or hem detail. Commission San Antonio paper and print artists instead of copying.

designCues.source: Dancehall and festival posters: bold condensed lettering, layered color
designCues.use: Inspiration for bilingual wordmarks and tee graphics. Have local designers draw original lettering.

designCues.cue: Accordion bellows and bajo sexto strings as line motifs
designCues.use: Abstract line graphics on socks, sleeves or lining, developed with a conjunto musician or cultural partner.

designCues.source: 1960s Westside records and Sir Douglas Quintet era sleeves
designCues.use: Retro label-style graphics on vintage-inspired tees. Clear any named artist.

productHooks: Fiesta-stripe City Edition extension: warm-up jacket, tee and cap in the magenta, marigold and turquoise stripe palette, with papel picado tonal detail.
Westside conjunto capsule with a San Antonio musician or poster artist, with credit, payment and a share of proceeds.
Bilingual Go Spurs Go tee and hoodie in Spanish and English, with gig-poster lettering.
Fiesta-week April drop timed to the playoff run, with a collectible medal-style pin or patch.
Rodeo-month western-leaning silhouette in black and silver with dancehall detail, for February.
watchouts: Selena Quintanilla's name, image and likeness are tightly controlled IP. Get an official license.
Don't lift sacred Dia de los Muertos imagery as costume or decoration. Partner with local artists and cultural groups.
Don't reduce San Antonio to one genre, or to Tejano alone. The market includes country, military, rock, hip-hop and international fans.
License and credit Fiesta San Antonio marks, medal designs and any named artist's work.
Mexican-American communities are not a monolith. Westside, Southside and South Texas border audiences differ.
